title: e-Kalyan Scholarship Jharkhand 2026: Apply Online ST/SC/BC
meta_description: e-Kalyan Jharkhand post-matric scholarship for ST, SC, BC students. Up to Rs 15,000+ per year via DBT. Apply at ekalyan.cgg.gov.in before July 31, 2026.

hero.one_liner: e-Kalyan is Jharkhand's post-matric scholarship for ST, SC, and BC students from Class 11 onwards. For families with income below Rs 2.5 lakh a year.

what_is_it: The e-Kalyan Post-Matric Scholarship is Jharkhand's main scholarship programme for Scheduled Tribe (ST), Scheduled Caste (SC), and Backward Class (BC) students pursuing education beyond Class 10. Applications are submitted exclusively through the online portal at ekalyan.cgg.gov.in, which is managed by the Centre for Good Governance (CGG) on behalf of the Welfare Department, Jharkhand.

The scholarship covers a wide range of post-matric courses including Class 11, Class 12, ITI, polytechnic diploma, undergraduate degrees (BA, BSc, BCom, BTech, MBBS, LLB, BCA, BBA), postgraduate courses (MA, MSc, MCom, MBA, MTech, MD), and PhD programmes. The student's course must be government-recognised and the institution must be on the approved list for the scholarship.

how_to_apply.title: Register on the portal
how_to_apply.description: Go to ekalyan.cgg.gov.in, click 'Student Login / Registration', and register using your Aadhaar number and Aadhaar-linked mobile number; an OTP will be sent for verification. Complete registration and note your login credentials for future access to track and update your application.

how_to_apply.title: Fill the application form
how_to_apply.description: Log in and select 'Post-Matric Scholarship' for your category (ST, SC, or BC). Fill in personal details, course details (institution name, course name, year of study), and family income details; verify all information carefully before proceeding to the next section.

how_to_apply.title: Upload documents
how_to_apply.description: Upload scanned copies of your caste certificate, income certificate, Jharkhand domicile certificate, Aadhaar card, qualifying examination mark sheet, and the fee receipt from your institution for the current academic year. All files must be in PDF or JPG format and within the specified size limit shown on the upload page.

how_to_apply.title: Submit and note application ID
how_to_apply.description: Review the complete application one final time, then click 'Submit' and note down the application ID generated; this ID is needed to track the application status at any point and you will also receive a confirmation SMS on your registered mobile number.

how_to_apply.title: Institutional verification
how_to_apply.description: After submission, the application moves to your college or institution for online verification. Inform your institution's scholarship coordinator about your submission so they verify your application promptly; delays at the institutional level can push the overall process past internal deadlines.

how_to_apply.title: District Welfare Officer approval and payment
how_to_apply.description: After institutional verification, the application goes to the District Welfare Officer (DWO) for sanction; once approved, the scholarship amount is disbursed via DBT to your Aadhaar-seeded bank account. Track the payment status on the ekalyan portal or confirm receipt via your bank statement or passbook.

extra_sections.heading: What the e-Kalyan Scholarship Is
content: Eligibility requires the student to be a domicile of Jharkhand and belong to the ST, SC, or BC category as certified by the competent authority. Family income must be below Rs 2.5 lakh per annum for ST and SC students, and some BC subcategories may have different income norms; students should check the current academic year's notification for their specific category.

The scholarship has two components: a maintenance allowance (paid monthly or quarterly) and a fee reimbursement component (covering actual tuition fees and non-refundable fees paid to the institution). The maintenance allowance rate depends on the course group and whether the student is a hosteller or a day scholar, as shown in the table above.

For 2026-27, the last date for both fresh applications (first-time applicants) and renewal applications (continuing students from previous years) is July 31, 2026. Students who miss this deadline may not receive the scholarship for the current year, so early application is strongly advised to allow time for document verification by the institution and the district welfare office.

The application process is entirely online through ekalyan.cgg.gov.in, where students register using their Aadhaar number and mobile number, fill in the application form, upload supporting documents, and submit the form. After submission, the application goes to the college/institution for verification, then to the District Welfare Officer (DWO), and finally to the state-level sanction and payment process.

extra_sections.heading: How Much You Get
content: Documents required for the e-Kalyan scholarship include the caste certificate (ST/SC/BC), income certificate from a competent authority (issued in the current or previous financial year), Jharkhand domicile certificate, Aadhaar card, bank account details (Aadhaar-linked, ABPS-enabled), mark sheet of qualifying examination (Class 10 or last exam passed), and the fee receipt from the current course institution.

Payment under the e-Kalyan scholarship is made via DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) using the Aadhaar-based Payment System (ABPS), which means the student's bank account must be linked to their Aadhaar number and must be ABPS-enabled. Students should verify this at their bank branch or through the NPCI portal before applying, as non-ABPS accounts will fail to receive payment even if the scholarship is sanctioned.

Renewal applications require the student to provide the mark sheet or result of the previous year's examination to prove they have passed and are eligible to continue; students who have failed are generally not eligible for renewal, though some categories may allow a grace period. The renewal process on the portal is similar to the fresh application but requires fewer new documents.

Students who passed their previous year's exam with low marks should still apply for renewal, as eligibility is based on passing and not on merit percentage for most post-matric scholarship categories. The cut-off is simply whether the student has passed and is enrolled in the next year of the same or a consecutive post-matric course.

extra_sections.title: Jharkhand's Main Post-Matric Scholarship
extra_sections.content:
e-Kalyan is the state's post-matric scholarship for ST, SC, and BC students. It covers courses from Class 11 onwards, including ITI, diploma, degree, and PG.

The amount depends on the course group and whether the student is a hosteller or a day scholar. The whole process is online.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: The e-Kalyan portal (ekalyan.cgg.gov.in) is also used for several other welfare schemes in Jharkhand including pre-matric scholarships, PVTG schemes, and some labour department schemes. Students should ensure they are applying to the correct post-matric scholarship link on the portal and not accidentally completing a pre-matric or other form.

A common issue that delays e-Kalyan scholarship payments is Aadhaar-bank seeding failure: even if the student has a bank account and an Aadhaar card, the scholarship amount cannot be transferred via ABPS unless the Aadhaar has been seeded to the specific bank account being used. Students should visit their bank at least 2-3 weeks before the application deadline to ensure Aadhaar seeding is done and ABPS is activated.

Students studying at institutions outside Jharkhand (in other states) can also apply for the e-Kalyan post-matric scholarship, provided the institution is government-recognised and the student otherwise meets all eligibility criteria. The scholarship amount is deposited into the student's Aadhaar-linked bank account regardless of where the institution is located.

The e-Kalyan scholarship for ST students is funded from the Tribal Welfare Department budget, for SC students from the Social Welfare Department, and for BC students from the Backward Classes Welfare Department. Despite these different funding streams, all three categories apply through the same ekalyan.cgg.gov.in portal, which consolidates the workflow for institutions and district officials.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply
content: The scholarship amount is credited in parts: typically the maintenance allowance is paid quarterly or as a lump sum at the start of the academic year depending on the state's release schedule, and the fee reimbursement is released separately after the institution submits the verified fee receipts to the district welfare office. Students sometimes experience a gap between when they pay fees and when the reimbursement arrives, so they should keep originals of all fee receipts.

To check the status of an e-Kalyan scholarship application, students can log in to their account at ekalyan.cgg.gov.in and view the application status under 'Application Status'. The portal shows at which stage the application currently is, whether at the institutional verification stage, the District Welfare Officer stage, or the payment sanctioned stage.

If the application is rejected by the institution or the DWO, the reason is typically communicated on the portal; common reasons include incomplete documents, income certificate exceeding the limit, Aadhaar seeding mismatch, or the student's course not being on the approved list. Students who believe a rejection was in error can correct the issue and reapply within the application window.

Keeping scanned copies of all documents in good quality before starting the application prevents most common rejection scenarios. A clear, readable income certificate issued in the current or immediately preceding financial year is especially important, as certificates more than a year old are often rejected by the DWO.

extra_sections.heading: The Income Ceiling and Course Groups
content: The e-Kalyan portal is sometimes slow or inaccessible close to the application deadline due to high traffic volume, as thousands of students from across Jharkhand submit applications simultaneously. Students are strongly advised not to wait until the last few days before the July 31 deadline and should complete their application at least two weeks in advance to avoid technical difficulties.

Students from the PVTG (Primitive Vulnerable Tribal Groups) communities of Jharkhand, such as the Asur, Birhore, Birija, Korwa, and Pahariya, may be eligible for additional scholarship benefits beyond the standard e-Kalyan rates. These students should check the PVTG-specific scholarship notifications on the portal and the Welfare Department website for the current year's special provisions.

extra_sections.heading: The Income Ceiling and Course Groups More
content: Beyond the e-Kalyan post-matric scholarship, Jharkhand also provides pre-matric scholarships (for Class 1 to 10) through the same departmental structure, and there are separate merit-based and career development scholarships for students pursuing specific professional courses. The e-Kalyan portal is the single gateway for all these schemes, and students should check all available scholarship types before submitting their application for the year.

The Jharkhand government has progressively digitised the entire e-Kalyan scholarship workflow, from application submission to final payment, reducing the scope for delays and corruption that existed in the earlier physical application system. Civil society organisations working with tribal students in Jharkhand have noted that the DBT payment mode through ABPS, while occasionally causing issues for first-time bank account holders, has significantly reduced scholarship diversion and has improved the rate at which eligible students actually receive their entitlement.

extra_sections.title: The Family Income Ceiling
extra_sections.desc:
The scholarship is for students whose family income is below Rs 2.5 lakh a year, so it reaches those who need it most.

The amount also depends on the course group and whether you live in a hostel or study as a day scholar.

extra_sections.heading: Documents and Deadlines
content: Students who face persistent issues with their e-Kalyan application, such as Aadhaar seeding failures or repeated rejection without clear reason, can approach the District Welfare Officer in their home district or the State Welfare Department in Ranchi for resolution. The Welfare Department also has a helpdesk accessible through the ekalyan.cgg.gov.in portal for technical queries related to the application process.

Girl students from ST and SC communities pursuing science, technology, engineering, or medical courses are especially encouraged to apply, as these categories receive the highest Group I maintenance allowance under the e-Kalyan scheme. The Jharkhand government has been actively working to increase the share of tribal women in professional education, and the scholarship serves as the key financial enabler for this goal.

Students who are enrolled in distance education programmes (correspondence courses) from recognised universities may also be eligible for the post-matric scholarship under certain categories. However, the maintenance allowance rates for distance learning students may differ from those for regular full-time students, and the course must be from a university listed on the University Grants Commission (UGC) approved list.

The scholarship covers courses in private aided colleges (receiving government aid) and private unaided colleges (self-financing institutions) that are on the approved institution list for the state's post-matric scholarship. Students at private unaided colleges typically receive the fee reimbursement component for actual fees up to a capped ceiling as notified by the state, rather than the full fee amount if it exceeds the ceiling.

extra_sections.heading: Renewing Each Year
content: Students belonging to both ST and SC categories simultaneously (which can happen in certain administrative reclassifications) should apply under the ST category for the e-Kalyan scholarship, as ST scholarship rates are generally the same or better. If there is any ambiguity about which category certificate to use, the student should consult the District Welfare Officer before submitting the application.

The National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and the e-Kalyan portal are two separate systems that sometimes cause confusion among students: the e-Kalyan portal at ekalyan.cgg.gov.in is specifically for Jharkhand state scholarships, while the NSP at scholarships.gov.in handles central government scholarships such as the National Overseas Scholarship and the Pre-Matric Scholarship for Minority Communities. Jharkhand students should use both portals as appropriate, since state and central scholarships are not mutually exclusive.

extra_sections.title: Apply Before the Last Date
extra_sections.content:
e-Kalyan opens for a window each year, so apply before the last date to avoid missing the whole year. Keep your documents scanned and ready.

Continuing students usually renew each year by updating their marks and admission details on the same portal.

extra_sections.heading: Renewing Each Year More
content: Students who are receiving the e-Kalyan post-matric scholarship can also simultaneously apply for central government scholarships such as the National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of ST Students (Top Class Scholarship) offered by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. These central schemes have separate eligibility criteria and portals, and receiving the state scholarship does not disqualify a student from applying for central scholarships as well.

The income certificate used for the e-Kalyan scholarship application must be issued by a competent authority, which in Jharkhand means the Circle Officer (CO) at the tehsil level or the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM). Income certificates from employers, bank managers, or other unofficial sources are not accepted; students should apply for the income certificate at the CO's office well in advance of the scholarship deadline as processing can take several weeks.

extra_sections.heading: Why the Scholarship Matters
content: For students pursuing professional courses such as MBBS, BTech, or LLB at institutions that charge high annual fees, the fee reimbursement component of the e-Kalyan scholarship can be the most significant part of the benefit. These students are advised to submit fee receipts promptly to their institution's scholarship coordinator, as delays in fee receipt submission at the institutional level are a common cause of late or incomplete scholarship payment.

Jharkhand's tribal belt districts such as Dumka, Pakur, Sahibganj, Godda, Khunti, West Singhbhum, and Simdega have some of the highest concentrations of e-Kalyan scholarship applicants. Given the relatively lower penetration of banking and digital literacy in these areas, the district welfare offices in these regions often set up special camps at colleges and block offices before the application deadline to help first-generation learners complete the online process.

extra_sections.heading: Why the Scholarship Matters More
content: Once the scholarship is sanctioned and the payment notification is received, students should check the credited amount in their bank account and compare it with the expected amount for their course group and hosteller/day scholar status. If there is a shortfall or no credit despite the sanction notification, the student should contact the District Welfare Office with the sanction order number and their bank account details to initiate a payment investigation.

Students applying for the e-Kalyan scholarship for the first time often find the process easier if they seek guidance from a senior student or a teacher at their institution who has gone through the process before. Many colleges in Jharkhand have a dedicated scholarship cell or a teacher in charge of scholarship matters who can guide new students through the portal, document upload requirements, and institutional verification workflow.

extra_sections.title: e-Kalyan in Context Notes
extra_sections.content: The e-Kalyan scholarship has played a meaningful role in improving the gross enrolment ratio (GER) of ST and SC students in higher education in Jharkhand over the past decade. By removing the financial barrier that forced many tribal students to drop out after Class 10, the scheme has enabled a generation of first-generation college students from interior Jharkhand to complete undergraduate and professional degrees that were previously out of reach for their families.

faqs.question: What is the e-Kalyan scholarship for Jharkhand students?
faqs.answer:
e-Kalyan is Jharkhand's post-matric scholarship for ST, SC, and BC students studying beyond Class 10. It covers a maintenance allowance (Rs 5,000 to Rs 15,000+ per year depending on course and hosteller/day scholar status) plus actual fee reimbursement.

Applications are at ekalyan.cgg.gov.in and the 2026-27 last date is July 31, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the last date for e-Kalyan scholarship 2026?
faqs.answer: The last date for both fresh and renewal applications for the 2026-27 academic year is July 31, 2026. Students are advised to apply well before this date as the portal experiences high traffic near the deadline.

faqs.question: What is the income limit for the e-Kalyan scholarship?
faqs.answer: Family income must be below Rs 2.5 lakh per annum for ST and SC students. BC students should check the current year's notification for their specific subcategory income norms, as these may differ slightly.

faqs.question: How much scholarship amount do e-Kalyan students get?
faqs.answer: The maintenance allowance ranges from Rs 120 per month (Group IV day scholar) to Rs 750 per month (Group I hosteller), paid for 10 months per year, plus actual tuition and non-refundable fee reimbursement. Total annual benefit varies by course and institution fees.

faqs.question: How is e-Kalyan scholarship paid?
faqs.answer:
Payment is via DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) using the Aadhaar-based Payment System (ABPS). The student's bank account must be Aadhaar-seeded and ABPS-enabled.

Students should confirm ABPS activation at their bank before applying.

faqs.question: Can students studying outside Jharkhand apply for e-Kalyan?
faqs.answer: Yes. Jharkhand-domicile ST, SC, and BC students studying at government-recognised institutions in other states can apply for the e-Kalyan post-matric scholarship, provided they meet all other eligibility criteria.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for e-Kalyan scholarship?
faqs.answer: Caste certificate (ST/SC/BC), income certificate (current financial year), Jharkhand domicile certificate, Aadhaar card, Aadhaar-linked bank account details, qualifying exam mark sheet, and institution fee receipt for the current year.

faqs.question: How do I check e-Kalyan application status?
faqs.answer: Log in to ekalyan.cgg.gov.in with your registered credentials and go to 'Application Status'. The portal shows the current stage of your application whether at institution verification, DWO approval, or payment disbursement.

faqs.question: What if my e-Kalyan application is rejected?
faqs.answer:
Log in to the portal to view the rejection reason. Common reasons are incomplete documents, income above the ceiling, Aadhaar seeding mismatch, or course not on the approved list.

Correct the issue and reapply within the application window.

faqs.question: Is the e-Kalyan scholarship available for ITI and polytechnic students?
faqs.answer: Yes. ITI and polytechnic diploma students fall under Group IV of the post-matric scholarship category and receive a maintenance allowance of Rs 230 per month (hosteller) or Rs 120 per month (day scholar), plus fee reimbursement for their course.
